chunks: From him, from Usman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When you pray the morning and the Maghrib prayers, say: 'In the Name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. There is neither might nor strength except with Allah, the Exalted, the Magnificent,' seven times, for whoever says it will not be struck by insanity, nor leprosy, nor vitiligo, nor seventy types of afflictions.

key_terms.بَرَصٌ: Vitiligo or white spots on the skin
key_terms.لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّه: There is no might and no power except with Allah (a key dhikr phrase)

ai.seo_question: What is the benefit of reciting 'La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah' seven times after morning and Maghrib prayers?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) prescribes reciting 'La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah al-'Ali al-'Azeem' seven times after Fajr and Maghrib prayers as a spiritual shield. It emphasizes divine sufficiency as a means of protection from both physical ailments like leprosy and mental afflictions such as insanity, reflecting the Shia emphasis on dhikr as a practical remedy for worldly and otherworldly trials.
